inputs.transcript: A: You say we need to move forward, but I cannot trust you unless I know what happened. B: I do not want to rehash trauma or confess forever. You did it too.
private_memory_a: A responds well to one-question prompts during trust discussions.
private_memory_b: B responds better to specific questions than global claims.
shared_memory: During escalation, use one question and one answer at a time.

observable_basis: A links moving forward to needing a specific trust answer.
B rejects open-ended confession and raises reciprocal trust injury.
Both speakers reference past injury without a bounded disclosure process.

loop_summary.name: pursuer-defender loop
loop_summary.without_blame: One partner fears that moving forward will erase accountability; the other fears that disclosure will become unlimited prosecution. The repair path is one decision-relevant question each.

participant_a.private_read: You appear to be trying to protect your ability to make informed choices.
participant_a.strongest_point: You are asking for clarity instead of guessing.
participant_a.risk_point: Global accusations make it harder to get the direct answer you want.
participant_a.what_the_other_person_is_probably_hearin: I am already guilty no matter how I answer.
participant_a.next_best_message: I agree that we should move forward. I also need one specific issue addressed so the reset is real. My question is: is there any current contact I need to know about? I am asking for a direct answer, not a full rehash. I also understand that mutual transparency has to apply to both of us.
participant_a.individual_exercise: Use the One Question Mirror: name one decision-relevant question, why it matters, the category of transparency, your answer to the same category, one boundary, and one behavior you will change.

covey_habit_focus.habit: Habit 5: Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood
covey_habit_focus.practical_reason: A narrow question improves the chance of receiving an answer before debating meaning.

participant_b.private_read: You appear to be trying to avoid being boxed into a vague accusation.
participant_b.strongest_point: You are asking for enough specificity to answer fairly.
participant_b.risk_point: Explaining why the accusation is unfair can sound like avoiding the question.
participant_b.what_the_other_person_is_probably_hearin: You are refusing to answer unless the question is perfect.
stop_doing_next_20_minutes: Do not counterattack the wording first.
Do not answer multiple implied accusations.
participant_b.next_best_message: I do not want us to relive trauma or turn this into blame shifting. I am willing to answer specific, decision-relevant questions in a structured way. I also need transparency to be mutual, not one-directional. Let’s each ask one specific question and answer it directly.
participant_b.individual_exercise: Use the One Question Mirror: name one decision-relevant question, why it matters, the category of transparency, your answer to the same category, one boundary, and one behavior you will change.

covey_habit_focus.practical_reason: Choosing a direct response interrupts defensiveness and keeps the exchange answerable.

covey_habit_map.participant_a: Habit 5: Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood
covey_habit_map.session_focus: Before reconciliation or future planning, define one decision-relevant question each and answer without graphic or punitive details.

prompts: The one question I want answered is: ____.
Why this question matters for repair is: ____.
The category of transparency I am asking for is: ____.
My answer to the same category of question would be: ____.
The boundary I need going forward is: ____.
The behavior I will change is: ____.

private_memory_a: A requests transparency but needs help converting it into one specific, decision-relevant question.
private_memory_b: B avoids trust discussions when they become global or punitive and responds better to bounded disclosure.
shared_memory: During trust repair, each person gets one decision-relevant question per session.
Transparency must be mutual and bounded.
No graphic details unless both agree they are necessary.

immediate_steps: Pause for 20 minutes if either person escalates.
Return with one question and one answer only.
reflection_prompts: What is the one answer I need or can give right now?
recommendations.next_session_goal: Complete the one-question, one-answer repair sequence without expanding into future planning.

mvp_product_recommendation: Build a Mutuality Check before any transparency message is sent, prompting users to convert confession demands or fresh-start avoidance into one bounded, reciprocal, decision-relevant question.

decision_relevant_questions.participant_a: Is there any current contact I need to know about?
decision_relevant_questions.participant_b: What same category of transparency are you willing to provide about your past conduct?

intervention_language: Transparency is valid. Unlimited confession is not.
Moving forward is valid. Avoiding accountability is not.
One question each. One answer each. Then pause.
